level1.text: An electric motor takes electrical energy of $400\,\text{J}$ and gives $340\,\text{J}$ of kinetic energy. What is the efficiency of the motor? Give the answer as a percentage.
An LED lamp takes a power of $8.0\,\text{W}$ from the electricity grid and gives a light power of $2.4\,\text{W}$. What is the efficiency of the lamp? Give the answer as a percentage.
The efficiency of an incandescent lamp is $5.0\,\%$, and the lamp takes a power of $60\,\text{W}$ from the electricity grid. How large is the light power given by the lamp? Give the answer in watts.
The efficiency of an electric motor is $90\,\%$, and it gives useful energy of $1800\,\text{J}$. How much electrical energy did the motor take? Give the answer in joules.
Radiation energy of $5.0\,\text{kJ}$ hits a solar panel, and the efficiency of the panel is $20\,\%$. How much energy becomes losses? Give the answer in kilojoules.

level2.text: An electric motor takes a power of $1.0\,\text{kW}$ from the electricity grid, and its efficiency is $80\,\%$. The motor runs for $2.0\,\text{min}$. How much kinetic energy does the motor give? Give the answer in kilojoules.

An LED lamp with an efficiency of $30\,\%$ takes a power of $9.0\,\text{W}$. An incandescent lamp with an efficiency of $5.0\,\%$ gives the same light power. How large a power does the incandescent lamp take from the electricity grid? Give the answer in watts.
An incandescent lamp with an electrical power of $60\,\text{W}$ and an efficiency of $5.0\,\%$ burns for $4.0\,\text{h}$. How much electrical energy becomes heat? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

The efficiency of the petrol engine of a car is $25\,\%$, and the engine gives a power of $15\,\text{kW}$ to move the car. How large is the loss power, that is, the power that becomes heat? Give the answer in kilowatts.

level3.text: Device A takes energy of $200\,\text{J}$ and gives useful energy of $150\,\text{J}$. Device B takes energy of $4.0\,\text{kJ}$, and its losses are $2.0\,\text{kJ}$. How many times as large is the efficiency of device A compared with the efficiency of device B?

A radiation power of $1.2\,\text{kW}$ hits a solar panel, and the efficiency of the panel is $20\,\%$. How long does the panel need to produce $0.50\,\text{MJ}$ of electrical energy? Give the answer in seconds.

An energy flow diagram is drawn to a scale in which the arrow of the energy entering the device is $6.0\,\text{cm}$ thick and corresponds to an energy of $240\,\text{J}$. The arrow of the useful energy is $1.5\,\text{cm}$ thick. How much energy becomes losses? Give the answer in joules.
